outcomes: Students will be able to describe the role of economics in corporations with regard to decision‐making and choice.

Students will be able to apply business and economic decision‐making tools and their significance (including an understanding and ability to explain how these tools are useful and came to be relied upon).
Students will be able to explain the connection between business, economics and the financial markets.

textbooks: Required - Textbook: Principles of Financial Accounting, Simga-Mugan, C., N. Hosal-Akman, 5th, McGrawHill
outcomes: Students will be able to define basic financial statements and generally accepted accounting principles.
Students will be able to perform simple book keeping and prepare basic financial statements.
Students will be able to identify major asset, liability, equity, revenue and expense items and explain how they are accounted for.
Students will be able to calculate and evaluate basic financial ratios of a business entity.
Students will be able to recognize Professional Code of Ethical Standards for accountants in Turkey and on the International Level.

3f6d15a703.fzText: Attending at least 75 per cent of the lectures and attaining the weighted minimum satisfactory scores of the assessment tools as announced by the course instructor.
weekly: Variability and Its Impact on Process Performance
textbooks: Required - Textbook: Matching Supply with Demand: An Introduction to Operations Management, Cachon and Terwiesch , 2024, McGraw-Hill
outcomes: Students will develop an understanding of the function and impact of operations in manufacturing and service organizations on the maintenance and sustainability of competitiveness, on value creation in society at large, and on the environment.
Students will get familiarized with experiences of domestic and international firms.
Students will be able to employ the tools/concepts of operations management to real problems.
Students will be equipped with the knowledge base to act as agents of change for operations management in organizations upon graduation.
Students will be able to identify the strategic issues in operations management.
Students will be able to identify the issues in quality management.
Students will be able to identify the issues in process design and analysis and compare the possible alternatives for design and development.
Students will be able to identify the issues in production/service system design and apply the basic analysis and solution tools in this area.
Students will be able to identify the issues in supply chain management and apply the basic decision models to problems in this area.
Students will be able to identify the issues at the interface of operation, finance and risk management.

weekly: Describing data: Graphs, tables, summary measures (Chapters 2,3)
Confidence interval estimation and hypothesis testing (Chapters 8-10)
Building linear programming (LP) models - Graphical method, Solver (Chapter 14)
LP applications continued, Data Envelopment Analysis (Chapter 15)
Non-linear optimization, multi-objective decision making continued(Chapter 14)
textbooks: Required - Textbook: Business Analytics Data Analysis & Decision Making, Albright SC, Winston WL, 2015, South-Western
outcomes: (1)Students wil be able to identify the need for quantitative managerial decision making tools to improve decision making in a business context and apply the appropriate tools.
(2)Students will be able to demonstrate an understanding of building blocks of quantitative managerial decision making models .

(3)Students will be able to build quantitative managerial decision making models which allow you to get maximum values from business strategies, recognize inherent assumptions, interpret the data and evaluate arguments when the firm has a single or multiple objectives and faces various constraints .
(4)Students will be able to solve and analyze quantitative decision making models using spreadsheets.
(5)Students will be able to analyze the best solution with respect to changes in the parameters of the problem, and evaluate solutions.

75682fbfc5.fzText: An FZ grade will be given to those students who have submitted less than 6 case memoranda throughout the semester and have accumulated a percentage grade point of less than 8 out of a total of 25 on participation. Additionally, those students who have a midterm exam grade of less than 20 out of 100 will also receive an FZ grade.

Evaluating start-up business plans, valuation of options, and cap tables
How VCs add value & VC deal terms
Later-stage deals, valuing convertible securities in late stages
Buyouts of family companies, impact of PE on firm performance
Financial restructuring; operational restructuring; secondary buyouts

Required - Lecture Notes: Lecture slides/notes and some articles posted on Moodle.
outcomes: Students will be able to understand the challenges that entrepreneurs face during their search for early-stage funding.
Students will be able to understand the similarities and differences of different investment sources such as angel investors, crowdfunding, venture capital funds, and buyout funds.
Students will be able to gain knowledge of key VC&PE terms and concepts
Students will be able to analyze a venture capital or buyout opportunity from a qualitative and quantitative perspective.
Students will be able to understand deal structure and term sheets.
Students will be able to understand the ways in which VC or PE investors can add value to the companies they invest in, and critically assess this ability in different contexts.
Students will be able to understand the challenges of fundraising in emerging markets.
Students will be to understand the funding structure of VC&PE partnerships.
Students will be able to evaluate the VC&PE fund investment opportunities from the perspective of institutional investors (a.k.a. limited partners in VC funds).

weekly: Marketing Communications Using Digital Media Channels - I
Marketing Communications Using Digital Media Channels - II
outcomes: Students will be able to demonstrate an understanding of the fundamentals of digital marketing, digital business models (e.g., freemium models), as well as digital ecosystems (e.g., online platforms).
Students will be able to explore/investigate and analyze several internal and external factors that may influence digital marketing strategies of firms.
Students will be able to develop digital marketing strategies that target customers via several marketing channels and technologies in a way that complements business goals as well as objectives.
Students will be able to analyze the role of digital marketing in the overall marketing mix and understand its impact on businesses and society at large.
Students will be able to develop an undertanding of how firms bulild and sustain data-driven relationship with customers in a digital setting.
Students will be able to have a solid understanding of several digital media channels and tools (e.g., SEO, SEM, social media, e-mail) and how to utilize them effectively.
Students will be able to assess the effectiveness of digital marketing campaigns via a range of metrics.
